restoration_note: The teaching enumerates the body's structural articulation as the dragon (enthumesis of body): seven sense-organs above (two eyes, two ears, two nostrils, one tongue) on the foremost-bust of the upper-man, seven members of the body below (paired and singular), and five 'caves' of the dragon (tongue, throat, heart, breath, bond) through which it gathers and casts forth. Most restorations are tightly constrained by visible traces, parallel formulas (the recurring 'ⲧⲥⲁϣϩⲃⲉ ⲛⲁⲡⲉ' / 'ⲡⲥⲁϣϥ ⲛⲁⲓⲥⲑⲏⲧⲏⲣⲓⲟⲛ' framing), and the symmetric upper-side / lower-side pairing. Genuine difficulties remain at gap 0 (3-char opener with no preceding context), gap 13 (10-char relative clause connector), gaps 23-24 (the unparalleled feminine-dual + singular members of the body's seven-fold list), and the wholly fragmentary section 4982 around 'ⲁⲣⲭⲱⲛ'. Gap 45 (6 chars between 'in them' and 'they shall call') is reconstructed conservatively as ⲧⲏⲣⲟⲩ.

coptic_restorations.basis: 3-char opener at section/line start preceding ⲧⲙⲛⲧⲉϩⲧⲉ. ⲉⲧⲉ ('namely / which is') is the most natural Lycopolitan filler that preserves the feminine determination of the following article (ⲧ-) and does not collide with the demonstrative ⲧⲁⲓ̈, which would absorb the article. Low confidence — could also be a closing copula '·' of a prior question.

english_segments.core_english: {0} the foremost-of-head itself, which is stretched upon
the dragon. These are: the seven sense-organs which are upon
the head of the body — namely, two are the places of seeing which
see in them; the two places of hearing which hear in
them; the place of smelling, two which smell in them; and the
tongue {1} which chooses in it, taking
in it the tastes which are varied, that exist in every likeness.
This is the seven-fold of head of the dragon — the seven sense-
organs which are upon the foremost-bust of the man of the upper side
and the man of the lower side. The seven-fold which are of the bo-
dy are these: the two {2}; the two haunches; the {3}
{4} archon {5}
the seven-fold of head which...
Heaven indeed and those below — they shall be perfected and act as foremost-
of-head over the dragon, his five caves which they have spoken
concerning them, that he gathers them inward and casts them forth upon them
by the dragon. They themselves are these: the first is the tongue;
the second is the throat; the third is the heart;
the fourth is the breath; the fifth is the bond which
is set within them, which also peers forth from them and
reveals his likeness forth, with the contemplation of the upper
side and the lower side, making a war in
his foremost-of-head. He who shall recognize them in
the body — and shall fight with her and prevail over her and slay
her in them {6}, they shall call to him

Renders proposed Coptic ⲛ̄ⲕⲓⲃⲉ as the feminine-dual first item of the body's seven-fold list. Low confidence — could equally be 'hands' (ⲛϭⲓϫ) or another paired feminine member.
